title: Fix it: read order lines from an xml order that may have one line, several, or none
basics: In XML, the same element name can repeat: `<line/><line/>`. `payload.order.line` selects only the first one; `payload.order.*line` selects all of them as an Array. Attributes are read with `@`, so `.@sku` is the value of the `sku` attribute.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

The ERP sends orders as XML:

```
<order id="7"><line sku="A" qty="2"/></order>
```

Return `{ orderId, lines }` where `lines` is an array of `{ sku, qty }` with `qty` as a Number. An order may have any number of lines, including none. With no lines, `lines` is an empty array.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.

cases.input: <order id="10"><line sku="C" qty="3"/><line sku="D" qty="1"/><line sku="E" qty="2"/></order>

hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
reads all lines but has no fallback, so an order without lines gives null instead of []

explanation.approach: A repeated XML element is several keys with the same name, and the single-value selector stops at the first. `.*` collects them all, which covers one and many alike. With none at all it gives null, and mapping null gives null, so a `default []` is needed for the empty order.

snippets.label: The single-value selector on two lines
snippets.note: Only the first line is read.

snippets.label: .* on an order with no lines
